Definition: from βραβεύς (an umpire of uncertain derivation); an award (of arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games:--prize.
BiblicalUsage: The word brabeîon is a prize in the public games. You meet it in 1 Corinthians, where it does exactly what it sounds like it should do.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that brabeîon shows God wastes no words — every word He gives, including this one, belongs where it is.
